The total outward electric displacement normal to the surface of the cube equals the total charge enclosed, by Gauss’s law for electric displacement \( \oint \mathbf{D} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = Q_{\text{enc}} \).  

The metal surface has radius 1 m and surface charge density \( \sigma = 20 \ \text{C/m}^2 \).  
Surface area of sphere: \( 4\pi r^2 = 4\pi (1)^2 = 4\pi \ \text{m}^2 \).  
Charge enclosed: \( Q = \sigma \times \text{area} = 20 \times 4\pi = 80\pi \ \text{C} \).  

Thus total outward electric displacement = \( 80\pi \ \text{C} \).  

Final answer: (B)
